title: Post-incident evidence verification checklist and customer-impact canonical
author: Marcus Nguyen
content:
Summary
This document codifies a single canonical checklist and verification flow for post-incident evidence collection, impact quantification, and customer-facing impact assertions. It is intended to be used by oncall engineers, incident commanders, and postmortem authors to: confirm SLO / error-budget effects, surface capacity drivers, validate operational tooling artifacts, and produce auditable evidence sets for legal, sales, and customer success.

Scope
- Applies to all SRE-managed incidents affecting production Redwood inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).
- Covers telemetry, traces, service configs, capacity allocations, and synthetic canary runs used to validate incident hypotheses.
- Does NOT replace runbook action steps during a live incident; this is post-incident verification and packaging guidance.

Principles (why this matters)
1. Single source of truth: every postmortem must reference an immutable evidence bundle that can be replayed or re-scored.
2. Reproducibility: anybody on the SRE team should be able to reproduce the key telemetry slices and have a deterministic snapshot of the environment that caused the issue.
3. Customer clarity: downstream impact statements (SLA credits, communications) must be traceable to metrics and queries in the bundle.

Owner and escalation
- Evidence steward (primary): oncall engineer who executed the incident triage (assign in incident doc).
- Verification lead (secondary): incident commander or assigned postmortem owner.
- Escalation: if evidence artifacts are incomplete, tag the owning service lead and the telemetry team. Slack channel: #sre-evidence.

Canonical evidence bundle (what to collect)
Collect the following artifacts, compress into evidence-bundle-<INCIDENT_ID>.tgz and store in artifacts.redwood/sre/evidence/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<INCIDENT_ID> with an SHA256 sum.
- Incident timeline: chronological CSV or JSON export of PagerDuty/Shelly events for the incident.
- SLO time series: 1s-aggregate timeseries (p50/p90/p95/p99/99.9) for affected SLOs covering -2h..+6h around incident start.
- Raw request sampling: 1:1000 full traces or 1:1 for incidents affecting correctness (max 10k). Redact PII according to data retention policy.
- Trace exports: at least 100 high-latency, 50 error-case and 50 success-case traces with full spans.
- Configuration snapshot: service config, autoscale settings, model instance image tags, quantization flags (eg: Q4, INT8), and routing policy at incident time.
- Capacity state: GPU pool headroom, warm model pools, warm-pool eviction logs, preemptible node events, and queue lengths.
- Deployment metadata: model version, container image digest, rollout stage, canary percentage.
- Synthetic canary runs: before/after synthetic queries using the canary harness for relevant prompt templates.
- Alerting rules & thresholds: copies of alert definitions that fired (exact versions).
- CLI / runbook commands executed: paste of terminal commands (timestamps), e.g., kubectl, redis, model-serving-admin.
- Observability links: Grafana dashboard snapshots (png), link to the dashboard, and Prometheus query text.
- Evidence manifest (REQUIRED): evidence-manifest.txt with a list of files and SHA256 checksums.

Verification checklist (step-by-step)
1. Bundle creation (evidence steward)
   a. Create evidence directory and place all artifacts listed above.
   b. Generate SHA256 checksums and evidence-manifest.txt.
   c. Upload to artifacts.redwood with ACL set to 'sre-read' and mark as immutable.
2. Sanity verification (verification lead)
   a. Confirm the timeline contains the incident start and the page/alert IDs.
   b. Run the SLO reproduction queries (examples below) and confirm numbers match the SLO time series file.
   c. Confirm at least one trace shows the high-latency/error path described in the timeline.
3. Capacity correlation (SRE oncall)
   a. Cross-check GPU headroom and warm pool metrics to the time windows.
   b. Validate any autoscaler activity logs; note whether burst autoscaling occurred and if requests queued.
4. Tooling evidence (telemetry engineer)
   a. Verify Grafana snapshots render and that Prometheus queries contained in the bundle return the same numeric series.
   b. Confirm alert definitions (by commit hash or config id) that fired are present.
5. Customer-impact statement (postmortem owner)
   a. Map the SLO breach window precisely and compute error-budget burn using the formula below.
   b. Create a short customer-facing summary (1–2 sentences) that references the evidence bundle path.
6. Closure: sign-off from service owner, security reviewer (if customer data was involved), and SRE verification lead.

SLO / error budget mapping (practical queries and formula)
- Query examples (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - P99 latency (service X): 
    sum(rate(latency_seconds_bucket{service=\"svc-x\",le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(latency_seconds_count{service=\"svc-x\"}[5m]))
  - Error rate (5xx): 
    sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"svc-x\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"svc-x\"}[5m]))
- Error budget calculation (example):
  - SLO: 99.9% successful requests per week -> allowable error budget = 0.1% of requests in a 1-week window.
  - Burned during incident = 1 - (observed_success_fraction / slo_target). Convert to percentage points and integrate across affected window.
- Tip: produce both absolute (requests impacted) and relative (percentage of weekly budget) numbers for customer communications.

Capacity analysis section (what to look for)
- Headroom vs sustained demand: compare headroom metric (free_gpu_seconds) to sustained QPS converted to tokens/sec using model-profile table.
- Warm pool churn: examine warm_pool_fill_rate, warm_pool_eviction_count, and model_warm_latency. If warm pool eviction preceded tail-latency spikes, document eviction cause (OOM, preemption, scaling policy).
- Multi-tenant contention: correlate tenant token_priority and priority-lane preemptions to observed latency regressions.

Operational tooling verification (concrete checks)
- Grafana: ensure png snapshot exists and contains time range -2h..+6h.
- Tracing: span sampling rate must be the value present in the trace-config at incident time.
- Autoscaler logs: verify controller events and HPA/VPA snapshots (or autoscale-controller logs).
- Model-serving admin: export of model cache sizes and KV cache hit/miss rates.
- Repro harness: run the provided synthetic script (./tools/canary/run.sh --start <TS> --end <TS>) in a staging env that mirrors the production patch; include raw outputs in the bundle.

Table: evidence-to-consumer mapping
| Evidence Artifact | Consumer | Use-case | Required? | Owner |
|-------------------|----------|----------|----------:|------|
| SLO time series CSV | Product / Legal | Quantify SLA impact | yes | infra-sre |
| Raw traces | Eng oncall | Root-cause analysis | yes | svc-team |
| Deployment metadata | Release engineering | Recreate faulty release | yes | release-eng |
| Warm pool logs | Platform | Capacity reasoning | conditional | infra-sre |
| Synthetic canary output | QA / CS | Validate fix | conditional | qa-eng |

Postmortem authoring expectations (timeline)
1. Draft postmortem: 72 hours after incident close. Include a one-paragraph customer impact and link to evidence bundle.
2. Verification and reviewer comments: within 1 week. All checklist items must be marked complete in the incident doc.
3. Public/Customer summary prepared after sign-off (by product/CS) and stored alongside evidence bundle.

Runbook fragment: reproducing a capacity-eviction scenario (minimal steps)
1. Identify suspect node set: kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=dynamic-gpu -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, allocatable:.status.allocatable}'
2. Export autoscaler events: kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/autoscaler --since=8h > autoscaler.log
3. Replay demand (staging): ./tools/stress/generate_tokens_load --qps 600 --duration 600 --model \"stable-7b\" --tenant-id test-tenant > replay.out
4. Collect warm-pool metrics: curl -s \"http://platform-metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=warm_pool_fill_rate\" > warm_pool.json
5. Compare traces: use trace-replay tool: ./tools/trace/replay --input traces/sample-trace.json --target staging

Quality gate: redaction and legal review
- If raw request samples contain customer text, run the redaction tool: ./tools/redact --input requests.json --policy pii-v2 --output requests-redacted.json.
- If customer PII was exposed, notify security@redwood and set confidentiality:restricted for the evidence bundle.

Automation and operational tooling roadmap items (recommended improvements)
- Automate evidence bundle generation in the incident close workflow with a single button in the incident doc.
- Add immutable artifact storage with automatic checksum verification.
- Implement a lightweight evidence lint tool that validates the presence of required artifacts and returns a pass/fail for the verification checklist.

Appendix: example evidence-manifest.txt format
# evidence-manifest.txt
version: 1
incident_id: RID-2024-407
collected_by: oncall@team
files:
- p99-series.csv sha256: 3b2f...
- traces/slow-trace-001.json sha256: 9a4b...
- grafana/svc-x-2024-11-12.png sha256: a1c2...

Contacts and links
- Evidence Slack channel: #sre-evidence
- Telemetry on-call: pagerduty schedule \"telemetry-oncall\"
- Artifact storage: artifacts.redwood/sre/evidence/<date>/<incident_id>
- Template postmortem: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/postmortem-template
